## 2. Summary

This part-time job contract is for AZIZ KARIMOV from September 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027, at 행복분식 in Seongnam, Gyeonggi-do. The hourly wage is 9,000 KRW, with no weekly rest day and no overtime pay. The contract does not provide a copy to the worker and includes deductions for uniform costs and a deposit. The worker must give one month's notice to quit and will lose 50% of their last month's pay if they do not.

## 3. Red flags

### 1. [HIGH] No weekly rest day or holiday pay

The contract says there is no weekly rest day (주휴일). Workers who work 15 hours or more per week are entitled to a paid weekly rest day (주휴수당).

> Korean: 5.근무일/휴일:매주월,화,수,목,금요일근무/주휴일:없음  (quote matched to scan: yes)

### 2. [HIGH] Hourly wage below the legal minimum

The hourly wage is 9,000 KRW. The legal minimum wage is 10,320 KRW per hour in 2026. Paying less is not allowed, even if you agree to it. Ask for a correction or contact the Ministry of Employment and Labor (call 1350).

> Korean: -시간급:9,000원  (quote matched to scan: yes)

- [ ] real problem  - [ ] not a problem (false alarm)  - [ ] explanation correct  - [ ] severity right

### 3. [HIGH] No social insurance

The employer does not enrol the worker in social insurance (national pension, health, employment, accident). Employers must do this for most workers, and missing insurance can also cause problems with your visa and health care.

> Korean: 8.사회보험 적용여부: 고용보험[]산재보험[] 국민연금[] 건강보험[](가입하지 않음)  (quote matched to scan: yes)

### 4. [HIGH] You do not get a copy of the contract

The employer must give you a copy of the signed contract (Labor Standards Act, article 17). Without a copy you cannot prove the wage, hours or duties. Ask for a signed copy, or take a photo of every page before you leave.

> Korean: 9.근로계약서교부: 본계약서는 사업주가 보관하며 근로자에게 교부하지 않는다  (quote matched to scan: yes)

### 5. [HIGH] The employer holds a deposit from you

The employer asks you to leave a deposit and decides alone whether to return it. Employers generally may not take money from a worker as a guarantee or penalty (Labor Standards Act, articles 20 and 22). Do not hand over cash without a receipt, and ask a labor office (1350) before you agree.

### 6. [MEDIUM] No overtime or night pay

The contract says overtime, night or holiday work is not paid extra. The law requires 50% extra pay for overtime, night work (22:00 to 06:00) and holiday work at workplaces with 5 or more employees. Saying it is 'included' in the hourly wage is not valid unless the wage clearly covers it.

## Baseline answer (same model, one plain prompt, for comparison)

This document is a short-term employment contract between a business owner and a foreign worker. Here's a plain English summary of the key points:

1. **Employment Period**: The contract starts on September 1, 2026, and ends on February 28, 2027.

2. **Workplace**: The job will be at a restaurant called 행복분식 (Happyness Fast Food) in Seongnam, Gyeonggi-do, Korea.

3. **Job Duties**: The worker will assist in the kitchen and perform any other tasks as directed by the employer.

4. **Working Hours**: The worker will work from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM, with no breaks.

5. **Work Days and Holidays**: The worker will work every Monday through Friday, with no holidays.

6. **Wages**: The hourly wage is 9,000 won, with no overtime or night work pay. Wages will be paid in cash on the last day of each month.

7. **Vacation**: There is no paid vacation.

8. **Insurance**: The worker will not be covered by any social insurance (employment, work injury, national pension, or health insurance).

9. **Contract Document**: The employer will keep the contract and not give a copy to the worker.

10. **Special Terms**:
    - If the worker wants to resign, they must give one month's notice. If they don't, 50% of their last month's pay will be deducted.
    - The worker must pay for any damage to uniforms or other items.
    - The worker must pay a 300,000 won deposit when they start work, which the employer will return at the end of the contract based on their judgment.
    - The worker must not disclose any work-related information to outsiders. If they do, they must compensate for any losses.
    - Any terms not mentioned in the contract will follow the employer's instructions.

**Risks**:
- **No Social Insurance**: This could mean the worker will not have access to government-provided health, pension, and work injury benefits.
- **No Vacation**: The worker will not receive paid time off.
- **No Notice Period for Resignation**: The worker must give one month's notice, and if they don't, they will lose a significant portion of their last month's pay.
- **No Deposit Refund Guarantee**: The employer has the discretion to decide whether to return the deposit, which could be risky.
- **No Legal Protections**: The contract does not provide legal protections for the worker, meaning the worker may not have the same rights as a regular employee.

It's important to discuss these terms with the employer or seek legal advice to ensure you understand all the implications.
